commitResults.messageBody:
Several assumptions the code relies on were only stated in Javadoc,
e.g. that TaskList indices are valid, that Parser receives an
already-stripped line, and that a TaskDateTime always has a date.
When one of these breaks, the program fails later and far from the
cause, or silently misbehaves (an unstripped 'bye ' is reported as
an unknown command).

Let's add assert statements at those points so a violated
assumption fails immediately, where the bug is. They cover:

* TaskList: valid index on get/mark/remove, non-null tasks
* Parser.parse: input is non-null and already stripped
* Storage, AddCommand, Task, Deadline, Event, TaskDateTime:
  arguments that callers always supply are non-null
* DeleteCommand: exactly one task is removed
* Myriad: a load error and skipped lines are never both reported

Only internal invariants are asserted. Conditions that user input or
a hand-edited save file can break, such as an event ending before
it starts or a blank description, stay as MyriadException checks,
since assertions may be disabled and must not replace error
handling.

Enable assertions for the Gradle run task, as the JVM ignores them
by default; the test task already enables them. Tests that fed
out-of-range indices or unstripped lines now expect AssertionError.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #2 from ryan24chua/branch-A-Assertions
commitResults.messageBody: Use assertions to document key assumptions

commitResults.messageTitle: Share startup messages between run and getGreeting
commitResults.messageBody:
run() and getGreeting() each showed the greeting followed by the same
two load-warning checks, written out twice. Duplicated logic like
this drifts: a new startup message added to one front end could
easily be forgotten in the other, so the console and the GUI would
greet the user differently.

Extract the block into showStartupMessages() and call it from both,
so there is one place that decides what a session opens with.

commitResults.messageTitle: Run each input line through one shared method
commitResults.messageBody:
run() and getResponse() each parsed the line, executed the command
and caught MyriadException to show it as an error, in two separately
maintained copies. The Javadoc promised that the console and the GUI
answer any line the same way, but only the duplicated code kept that
promise; changing error handling in one copy would silently break it.

Extract the shared steps into executeLine(), which returns whether
the command asked to exit. Each front end keeps only what genuinely
differs: run() loops and says goodbye after the loop, while
getResponse() adds the farewell to its reply and records the exit
request for the GUI.

commitResults.messageTitle: Define default data file path in one place
commitResults.messageBody:
The console entry point (Myriad.main) and the GUI (Main) each built
the path data/myriad.txt from their own copy of the same literal.
Both front ends must use the same file so they share one saved task
list, but nothing enforced that: editing one copy would quietly split
them onto different files.

Name the path once as Myriad.DEFAULT_DATA_FILE and use the constant
in both places. A named constant also says what the path is for,
which a bare 'data', 'myriad.txt' pair at the call site did not.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace magic window sizes with named constants
commitResults.messageBody:
Main set the window's minimum size with the bare literals 220.0 and
417.0. A reader had to recall JavaFX's setMinHeight/setMinWidth
signatures to know what the numbers mean, and a later tweak to the
window size would mean hunting through start() for them.

Name them MIN_WINDOW_HEIGHT and MIN_WINDOW_WIDTH at the top of the
class, where the window's fixed dimensions can be seen and adjusted
together.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update comments that name a removed method
commitResults.messageBody:
The class comments of Myriad and Command said that commands are run
and their errors caught in Myriad.readCommands(). No method by that
name exists any more; that job is done by executeLine(), which both
the console loop and the GUI go through.

Comments that name code which no longer exists send readers looking
for it and make them doubt the rest of the documentation. Point them
at executeLine() instead, and say 'Myriad' rather than 'the loop',
since the GUI has no loop.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split the input line once in Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
parse() split the line on whitespace to get the command keyword, then
called extractArguments(), which split the same line with the same
regex again to get the arguments. The two splits had to stay in step:
changing the pattern in one but not the other would make the keyword
and its arguments disagree about where the line divides.

Split once in parse() and take the keyword and arguments from the
same result, removing extractArguments(). This is simpler, and there
is now only one place that decides how a line is divided.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename look-alike variable in parseTaskNumber
commitResults.messageBody:
parseTaskNumber took a parameter named args and stripped it into a
local named arg. Names that differ by one letter are easy to misread
and to mistype, and since both are Strings the compiler would not
flag using one in place of the other.

Rename the local to numberText, which also says what it holds: the
text that should parse as a task number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename Ui.LINE to DIVIDER
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui names the rule it prints above and below every console message
LINE, while its own comments call it a divider. 'Line' is also the
word used throughout the code for a line of user input or of the
data file, so the constant's name suggests the wrong thing.

Rename it DIVIDER, matching how the comments describe it, and give
it a Javadoc. UiTest keeps its own copy of the rule to check console
output, so rename that copy too to keep the two recognisably alike.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share task type codes between tasks and Storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Each task's save-format line starts with a type letter, T, D or E.
The letters were written out twice: once in ToDo, Deadline and
Event's toSaveFormat() for saving, and again as case labels in
Storage.parseLine for loading. The two sides must agree exactly, but
nothing tied them together; a typo or a change on one side would
make every task of that type fail to load, and only at runtime.

Give each task class a TYPE_CODE constant, use it in toSaveFormat(),
and switch on the same constants in Storage. Both directions now
read the one definition, and the letters sit next to the class they
identify. The saved format is unchanged, so existing data files
still load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add type code and overlap check to Task hierarchy
commitResults.messageBody:
Prepare Task and its subclasses for the upcoming stats command,
which needs to count tasks by type and find ones due soon.

- Task gains isDone(), abstract getTypeCode(), and overlaps(from, to)
  (default false, like occursDuring).
- ToDo/Deadline/Event override getTypeCode() with their TYPE_CODE;
  Deadline/Event override overlaps() via TaskDateTime.rangesOverlap.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add stats query methods to TaskList
commitResults.messageBody:
Prepare TaskList for the 'stats' command: per-type task lists,
tasks due within a window, and the first N undone tasks.

- getTasksOfType(typeCode) — fresh list matching a TYPE_CODE.
- getTasksDueWithin(date, days) — overlap with [date, date+days],
  end-of-day inclusive, matching TaskDateTime.rangeEnd()'s convention.
- getOldestUndone(limit) — first limit undone tasks in add order.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add stats command
commitResults.messageBody:
Wire up the 'stats' command end to end: StatsCommand gathers the
per-type counts, due-soon tasks and oldest undone tasks from
TaskList, and Ui.showStats renders them (numbered lists reusing
formatNumberedTasks, 'none' when a section is empty).

commitResults.messageTitle: Recognize 'stats' as a command
commitResults.messageBody:
Wire 'stats' into the command language: matched like 'list' (no
args allowed), dispatches to StatsCommand, and listed in the
unrecognized-command help text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for the stats command
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover the new TaskList query methods (getTasksOfType,
getTasksDueWithin, getOldestUndone) and Parser's 'stats' dispatch,
including the day-7/day-8 boundary and no-args rejection. Also
fixes MyriadTest's unrecognized-command message assertion, which
still pinned the pre-'stats' wording and would otherwise have
been a silently stale test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #4 from ryan24chua/branch-C-Statistics
commitResults.messageBody: Branch c statistics

commitResults.messageTitle: Use JUnit BOM to align test dependency versions
commitResults.messageBody:
The JUnit Jupiter artifacts took their version from jUnitVersion, but
the platform launcher was pinned separately as '1.14.4', because the
platform uses 1.x numbering while Jupiter uses 5.x. Bumping JUnit meant
remembering to bump both, and a mismatch fails only at test run time.

Import the JUnit BOM and let it supply every JUnit artifact's version.
The resolved versions are unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JaCoCo test coverage report
commitResults.messageBody:
The testing target is coverage of the highest-value methods, but the
build had no way to measure coverage, so gaps could only be found by
reading the tests.

Apply the JaCoCo plugin and generate its HTML and XML reports after
every test run. Pin the tool to 0.8.14, the first release that supports
Java 25 class files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Set UTF-8 source encoding and enable lint
commitResults.messageBody:
The build left the source encoding to the JDK default, although Ui's
banner is written in box-drawing characters. javac also showed only
its default warnings, so other problems went unreported.

Compile with UTF-8 encoding and -Xlint:all -Werror, so every warning
fails the build instead of scrolling past. The one warning this
turned up, MyriadException lacking a serialVersionUID, is fixed here.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let StatsCommand take the date it reports on
commitResults.messageBody:
StatsCommand read LocalDate.now() in its constructor, so the 'due in
the next 7 days' section depended on the day a test ran and
execute() had no tests.

Add a constructor taking the date, with the no-argument one passing
today's date, and add StatsCommandTest to pin the report's content.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add execute tests for task-changing commands
commitResults.messageBody:
AddCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand and DeleteCommand had no tests
of their own; only their argument parsing and index check were
tested. The upcoming refactoring touches TaskList, Storage and Ui,
which all four depend on.

Add a test class for each, checking the list change, the reply, the
saved file, and that a rejected task number changes and saves nothing.
AddCommandTest also checks that a failed save keeps the added task.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move TaskList into the task package
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList sat in the root myriad package alongside Parser, Storage and
Ui, although it holds and queries Task objects and depends on nothing
but the task package. The root package mixed the task model with
parsing, storage and presentation.

Move TaskList and its test into myriad.task, next to the classes it
manages. Only package and import lines change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move Parser into a parser package
commitResults.messageBody:
Parser sat in the root myriad package, although turning typed input
into commands is a concern of its own, separate from the session
wiring in Myriad.

Move Parser and its test into myriad.parser. Only package and import
lines change, apart from AGENTS.md, whose example test path pointed
at the old location.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move Storage classes into a storage package
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage and LoadResult sat in the root myriad package, although
reading and writing the data file is a concern of its own, and
LoadResult exists only as the return type of Storage.load().

Move both, and StorageTest, into myriad.storage. Only package and
import lines change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move UI classes into a ui package
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui, MainWindow, DialogBox and Main sat in the root myriad package
beside the session wiring. Together they are everything that talks to
the user, through the console or the JavaFX window.

Move them, and UiTest, into myriad.ui. Only package and import lines
change, apart from MainWindow.fxml, which names its controller class
by its fully qualified name and would otherwise fail at startup.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make Task fields private and final
commitResults.messageBody:
Task exposed description and isDone as protected, so any subclass or
class in myriad.task could change them without going through setDone.
No class did, and description never changes after construction.
Deadline and Event also left their date fields non-final, and named
them date, startDate and endDate although each may hold a time too.

Make Task's fields private, with description final, and make the
Deadline and Event fields final. Rename them to by, start and end, to
match the /by, /from and /to markers the user types.

commitResults.messageTitle: Derive occursDuring from overlaps in Task
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and Event each overrode both occursDuring and overlaps, and
each occursDuring did what its overlaps already did with the query's
range passed in. The overlap rule was written four times, so 'show'
and 'stats' could drift apart on when a task takes place.

Define occursDuring once, as a final method in Task that calls
overlaps, and remove the overrides. Add DeadlineTest and EventTest to
pin the boundary cases that were only covered indirectly through
TaskListTest.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fold case with Locale.ROOT in find
commitResults.messageBody:
Task.descriptionContains lower-cased both the description and the
keyword with the default locale. Case rules differ between locales:
in Turkish, 'I' lower-cases to a dotless 'ı', so 'find TITLE' missed
a task described as 'title' on a machine set to that locale.

Lower-case both sides with Locale.ROOT, so matching is the same on
every machine. Add TaskTest, including a case run under a Turkish
default locale that fails without this change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace task type code strings with an enum
commitResults.messageBody:
Each Task subclass declared its save-format code as a String constant,
and TaskList, StatsCommand and Storage passed those strings around.
Any String could stand for a type, and Storage's switch needed a
default branch, so a new type left unhandled failed only at runtime.

Add a TaskType enum holding the three types and their codes, and use
it in their place. Storage now switches over TaskType with no default
branch, so the compiler checks that every type is handled. The save
format and error messages are unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Return read-only lists from TaskList
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList.asList() returned its backing ArrayList, so any caller could
add, remove or clear tasks without going through TaskList, a known
limitation the tests had pinned. The query methods returned
ArrayList too, tying callers to that implementation.

Return List<Task> throughout. asList() now gives a live read-only
view, and each query a read-only list of its matches, so tasks can
only be changed through TaskList's own methods. Replace the tests
that pinned the old mutable behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share one filter helper across TaskList queries
commitResults.messageBody:
Four TaskList query methods repeated the same loop, differing only in
the condition each task was tested against, and getOldestUndone added
a manual counter to the same pattern.

Add a private filter method that takes the condition as a Predicate
and collects matches with a stream, and reduce each query to one
call. getOldestUndone uses the stream's limit instead of its counter,
and now asserts that the limit is not negative, which Stream.limit
would otherwise reject with an exception of its own.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add TaskList.isEmpty for empty-list checks
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskNumberCommand checked for an empty task list with size() == 0,
because TaskList offered no direct way to ask.

Add isEmpty, the name the Java collections use for the same question,
and use it there.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace Parser if-else chain with a switch
commitResults.messageBody:
Parser.parse matched the first word against each keyword in turn with
equalsIgnoreCase, in an 11-branch if-else chain that repeated
'&& args.isEmpty()' for each command taking no arguments.

Lower-case the keyword once with Locale.ROOT and dispatch with a
switch, one case per keyword. Commands taking no arguments go through
a shared requireNoArguments check, and the unrecognised-command error
is built in one place.

Unlike equalsIgnoreCase, this no longer treats lookalike letters such
as the Turkish dotted 'İ' or the long 'ſ' as 'i' or 's', so 'lİst' is
now rejected like any unknown command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Precompile quoted marker patterns in Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
Parser split deadline and event arguments with String.split, building
the regex from the marker text on every call. The marker was pasted
into the regex unquoted, which worked only because '/by', '/from' and
'/to' contain no regex metacharacters.

Compile one Pattern per marker when the class loads, quoting the
marker so it always matches literally. Matching is unchanged: still
case-insensitive, and still absorbing the whitespace around the
marker.

commitResults.messageTitle: Read and write data file with java.nio
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage used File, Scanner and FileWriter. Scanner stops at the first
byte that isn't valid UTF-8 and hides the error, so a data file
re-saved in another encoding loaded as empty with no warning, and the
next save overwrote it. Scanner also splits lines on U+2028 and
U+0085, so a description containing either was cut in two on reload.
File.mkdirs reported failure only through an ignored return value.

Read the file with Files.readAllBytes, decode it as UTF-8 with bad
bytes replaced, and split it only on \n, \r\n and \r. Write it with
Files.createDirectories and Files.writeString in UTF-8. The bytes
written and the handling of well-formed files are unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Write data file atomically via a temp file
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage.save truncated the data file and then wrote the new contents
into it. A crash, power cut or full disk between the two left the
file empty or half-written, losing every task at the next launch.

Write the contents to a sibling .tmp file, flushed to disk with SYNC,
and move it over the data file with an atomic move, so the file is
always either the old list or the new one. If the write or move
fails, the temp file is removed and the data file is left untouched.
The temp file's fixed name means one left by a crash is reused by
the next save rather than accumulating.

commitResults.messageTitle: Group stats report data into a record
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui.showStats took five separate List<Task> parameters, which are easy
to pass in the wrong order, and wrote '7 days' into its text while
StatsCommand.DUE_SOON_DAYS defined the same number.

Pass a TaskStats record instead. It also carries the day count, so the
report prints whatever window the command used. TaskStats lives in
myriad.task rather than myriad.command so that ui does not start
importing command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove unused Ui no-arg constructor
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui() only delegated to Ui(true), and nothing calls it: Myriad and
every test construct Ui with an explicit isEchoingToConsole flag.
Removing it leaves one way to create a Ui, so readers do not have to
wonder which constructor a console session is meant to use.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract data loading from Myriad constructor
commitResults.messageBody:
The constructor juggled three temporaries in a try/catch to load the
saved tasks, which buried the session setup it exists to do.

Move the load into loadSavedData, which returns a small LoadedData
record: a helper cannot assign the constructor's final fields, and a
record keeps them final. Greeting and warning order are unchanged.

Add tests for an unreadable data file and for valid lines still
loading beside a bad one, since neither path was covered before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fail fast when an FXML layout fails to load
commitResults.messageBody:
DialogBox and Main caught IOException from FXMLLoader, printed the
stack trace and carried on. DialogBox then failed later with a
NullPointerException on its unset dialog label, hiding the real
cause, and Main left the program running with no window.

Throw IllegalStateException wrapping the original exception instead,
so a broken build stops at once with the actual reason. The layouts
ship inside the jar, so this only fires on a broken build.

commitResults.messageTitle: Trim historical notes from Javadoc comments
commitResults.messageBody:
Several comments described how the code used to be, e.g. Ui's framing
'used to be repeated' in Myriad, rather than why it is the way it is
now. Others had gone stale: Storage.load still pointed at the Myriad
constructor after loading moved to loadSavedData, and the Myriad and
TaskList class comments listed only some of the commands and
operations.

Remove the history, keep the design reasons, and fix the stale text.
Mark referenced names with {@link} where they resolve and {@code}
otherwise, so broken references show up in javadoc and code reads as
code. Only comments change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Track whether the last reply was an error
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI receives each reply as plain text, so it cannot tell a
rejected command apart from an ordinary answer, and errors are easy to
miss in a long transcript.

Record in Myriad whether the latest getResponse call ended in an
error, in the same way isExitRequested records an exit, so that the GUI
can highlight errors. A flag keeps getResponse's String return type,
which every existing caller and test relies on.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report whether saved data failed to load
commitResults.messageBody:
When the data file, or some of its lines, cannot be loaded, the warning
is appended to the greeting text, so the GUI shows it like any other
greeting and the user may not notice that tasks are missing.

Add Myriad.hasLoadProblem so the GUI can show such a greeting in a
warning style.

commitResults.messageTitle: Highlight error replies in the chat window
commitResults.messageBody:
Error replies looked the same as ordinary replies, so a mistyped
command was easy to overlook.

Show them in a pale red bubble with a thick red left edge. The edge
means an error does not depend on colour alone to stand out.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show saved-data warnings in a warning style
commitResults.messageBody:
A greeting that reports unreadable saved data looked like a normal
greeting.

Show it in amber instead. It uses a different colour from the red of
errors, because the user did nothing wrong, but it should still catch
the eye.

commitResults.messageTitle: Drop user avatar and shrink Myriad's avatar
commitResults.messageBody:
Both speakers were drawn the same way, each with an 80px picture,
although a chat with an app is not a chat between equals. The pictures
took about a quarter of the width in a window that is usually small,
and replies can be long.

Make the layout asymmetric:
* the user's commands become compact right-aligned bubbles with no
  picture, capped at 80% of the width
* Myriad's replies keep a 32px avatar on the left and may use the rest
  of the width

The unused user picture is removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tighten chat spacing and font sizes
commitResults.messageBody:
The bubbles used more vertical padding than needed, and the text-width
cap also counted the bubble's own insets, which a Label's width already
includes. Replies therefore stopped well short of the right edge.

Reduce the padding, correct the width allowance so replies use the
available width, and raise the text to 14px with slight line spacing
so that task lists are easier to scan.

commitResults.messageTitle: Lay out main window with VBox and HBox
commitResults.messageBody:
The main window placed the transcript and input row with fixed
AnchorPane offsets, so the two were coupled by a hard-coded 41px gap,
and the window could not be made narrower than 417px.

Stack the transcript and input row in a VBox, with the transcript
taking all spare height and the text field all spare width. Resizing
now needs no magic numbers, and the minimum width drops to 300px now
that the avatars are smaller. The scroll bar appears only when needed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command history for recalling input
commitResults.messageBody:
Retyping a command to fix a small mistake, or to repeat it, is tedious.
A shell-style history lets the user recall earlier commands instead.

Add CommandHistory, which keeps sent commands and a cursor for stepping
through them. It skips blank lines and consecutive repeats. It has no
JavaFX dependency, so its cursor logic is covered by JUnit tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Recall previous commands with Up and Down keys
commitResults.messageBody:
Connect CommandHistory to the text field: Up shows an older command,
and Down shows a newer one, then an empty line. The caret moves to the
end so the recalled command can be edited at once. Down does nothing
when the user is not browsing, so it never erases a line being typed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let the user scroll back through the transcript
commitResults.messageBody:
The transcript's scroll position was bound to its height to keep the
newest message in view. A bound property cannot be changed by anything
else, so the mouse wheel and scroll bar could not move it, and earlier
replies could not be read again.

Scroll to the bottom from a listener on the transcript's height
instead. New messages still come into view, and the user can scroll
freely between them.
